completeness.why: The new getExpectedAmount decides number vs range (and getScheduledAmount delegates to it), so normalizeSchedule, whose null case was already excluded upstream, is full; updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keep their own `== null ? 0 :` dispatch although the existing getScheduledAmount decides all three cases, so they are partial; the budget template's halving copy is not touched, presumably to keep its different rounding, instead of carrying that as an explicit variation, so it is none.

interface.why: getExpectedAmount takes just the amount, with no speculative options, but it introduces a second public helper next to the existing getScheduledAmount instead of using it, leaves the missing-amount case outside the definition, and does not make the template's halve-the-rounded-sum inconsistency explicit as a parameter.

disguised_duplication.where: The midpoint formula now exists once (getScheduledAmount delegates to getExpectedAmount); the remaining repetition is the undisguised `== null ? 0 :` guard at three sites and the untouched template copy in server/budget/schedule-template.ts.
